facts.statement: Waimanu lived during the Paleocene epoch, approximately 62 to 60 million years ago, shortly after the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event.
facts.quote: Waimanu is a genus of early penguin which lived during the Paleocene, soon after the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event, around 62–60 million years ago.

facts.statement: Waimanu likely had the body shape of a flightless loon or diver and may have moved like the great auk.
facts.quote: It may have resembled a flightless loon or diver in body shape, and possibly the great auk in its manner of locomotion.

facts.statement: Although Waimanu was probably flightless with wings specialized for diving, its wing bones lacked the extreme aquatic adaptations seen in modern penguins.
facts.quote: although it was probably flightless like all modern penguins, with wings specialized for wing-propelled diving, its wing bones do not yet show the extreme specializations modern penguins have for an aquatic lifestyle.

facts.statement: Waimanu was discovered in 1980 in the Basal Waipara Greensand near the Waipara River in Canterbury, New Zealand.
facts.quote: Waimanu was discovered in the Basal Waipara Greensand near the Waipara River, in Canterbury, New Zealand, in 1980.

facts.statement: The holotype of Waimanu is a partial skeleton containing an almost complete right tibiotarsus, part of a fibula, a tarsometatarsus, a pelvis, a synsacrum, and four tail vertebrae.
facts.quote: The holotype is a partial skeleton consisting of an almost complete right tibiotarsus, a proximal half of the right fibula, a right tarsometatarsus, a right pelvis, a synsacrum (with the last thoracic vertebra attached to the synsacrum), and four caudal vertebrae.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Waimanu is currently held at the Canterbury Museum in Christchurch, New Zealand.
facts.quote: It is held in the Canterbury Museum in Christchurch, New Zealand.

facts.statement: The genus name Waimanu is derived from the Māori words for "water" and "bird".
facts.quote: The genus name Waimanu comes from the Māori wai for "water" and manu for "bird".

facts.statement: The species Waimanu manneringi was named in honor of Al Mannering, who discovered and collected the holotype specimen.
facts.quote: One species is known, W. manneringi, named for Al Mannering who found and collected the holotype specimen.

facts.statement: Discovered in New Zealand in 1980, the name Waimanu comes from the Māori term for "aquatic bird".
facts.quote: Descubierto en Nueva Zelanda en 1980, el nombre Waimanu viene del término maorí para "ave acuática".

facts.statement: Waimanu is a genus of primitive penguin that lived shortly after the Cretaceous-Tertiary mass extinction.
facts.quote: Waimanu es un género de pingüino primitivo que vivió poco después de la extinción masiva del Cretácico-Terciario.

facts.statement: Waimanu manneringi lived in the mid-Paleocene, approximately 61 million years ago.
facts.quote: Waimanu manneringi, nombrada en honor a su descubridor Al Mannering, de mediados del Paleoceno hace cerca de 61 millones de años

facts.statement: Waimanu tuatahi lived in the late Paleocene, perhaps around 58 million years ago.
facts.quote: el menor Waimanu tuatahi de finales del Paleoceno, quizás hace unos 58 millones de años.

facts.statement: The genus Waimanu was described by Jones, Ando, and Fordyce in 2006.
The genus Waimanu includes the type species W. manneringi and the species W. tuatahi.
facts.quote: subdivision: W. manneringi Jones, Ando & Fordyce, 2006 (especie tipo) W. tuatahi Ando, Jones & Fordyce, 2006

facts.statement: Waimanu belongs to the order Sphenisciformes, which includes modern penguins.
Waimanu lived from the Selandian to the Thanetian stages, between 61.66 and 56 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Selandian to Thanetian (61.66 to 56 million years ago)

facts.statement: Waimanu provides evidence for the debate regarding whether modern birds (Neoaves) radiated before or immediately after the extinction of non-avian dinosaurs.
facts.quote: The discovery of Waimanu provided evidence for debate about whether the radiation of modern birds, Neoaves, took place before the extinction of the non-avian dinosaurs or extremely rapidly immediately after.

facts.statement: The discovery of Waimanu supports the idea that Neoaves radiated either shortly before the extinction of non-avian dinosaurs or extremely rapidly afterward in geological terms.
facts.quote: Su descubrimiento ayudó a apoyar la idea de que la radiación de las Neoaves (incluyendo a muchas de las aves modernas) tomó lugar poco antes de la extinción de los dinosaurios no avianos, o que esta debió de ser extremadamente rápida en términos geológicos.

rejected.statement: Waimanu was about the size of an emperor penguin, measuring approximately 1 meter (3.3 feet) in length.
rejected.quote: It was about the size of an emperor penguin (1 metre (3.3 ft)).
